answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A ember delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A prism check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A vine penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 9859 identities need 9859 bonds of 59 tokens, 24481 dollars of hardware and 45 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
